## Historical audit — S0090

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/external/fixed_h0/selected/external/bw_0005/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 is visible. Citations below refer to this file; offsets are character ranges of the supplied observations.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Student model request, line 18 [0,168693) | **Goal, not verified result:** reconstruct a Montessori classroom from one photograph, matching layout and viewpoint, with windows, low shelves, child-sized furniture, warm materials and daylight. The fixed runner, rather than the program, owns saving and rendering. |
| Student programs and runner feedback, line 18 [0,168693) | The first program specified multiple separate scene elements: walls, floorboards, five windows, cabinets, tables, stools, chairs, rug and small materials. Furniture assets grouped separate panels, legs and seats; grouping is not proof of geometrically correct contact. It specified wood-colored materials and procedural bump grain. Step 1 failed technically because `scene.world` was `None`. |
| Student revision and step 2, line 18 [0,168693) | The student created a world when absent and revised details and camera. The runner reported `ok: true`, rendered 16 samples, and saved a PNG and `scene.blend`. This establishes execution, not reference fidelity. |
| Student revision and step 3, line 18 [0,168693) | After the step-2 image was supplied, the student changed the camera from `(6.6,-10.4,5.0)`, lens 40, to `(3.5,-5.5,2.75)`, lens 27; extended walls, added a ceiling, darkened finishes and reduced lighting. The runner again reported success, 16 samples, a PNG and a blend file. These are executed changes, not proof that framing, lighting or materials improved. |
| Student session and response, lines 19 [0,3814), 20 [0,342) | The final read-only session received staged reference and two render images; its recorded tool calls were zero. The student replied `DONE` after step 3, with no executions remaining. No independent visual or geometric assessment is present. |

**Teacher input and autonomy:** No teacher message, diagnosis, proposed update, or adoption is visible in this chunk. The observed feedback is runner error/output and image delivery, not teacher instruction. The student independently revised code after the error and a supplied render; the trace does not expose the reasoning behind the visual revision.

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Execution succeeded on steps 2 and 3 after an initial technical failure; the final student response was `DONE`. Overall reconstruction correctness remains **unknown**, not formal visual success. The audit cannot inspect the referenced images or unseen chunk. Object placement, occlusion, part connections, camera pose, grain appearance, daylight quality and render artifacts therefore remain unverified; no human pose is specified in the visible code. In particular, whether the darker, wider third view better matches the photograph is an unresolved hypothesis. The program requested 64 samples, but the visible runner used 16; final resolution and image quality are not established by the log.

**Lessons:** Transferably, distinguish a repaired runtime failure and saved artifact from scene fidelity, and compare executed revisions against actual renders. The specific world initialization, classroom geometry, camera values and lighting adjustments are task-specific observations, not validated general solutions.
